findings.evidence: Diff lines 96-120: the only `hf.` projections used are `contDiffOn.continuousOn`, `nonneg`, `isCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi`, and `contDiffOn.mono Ioi_subset_Ici_self`; the last is implied by `IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.contDiffOn` (Basic.lean:283). `IsCompletelyMonotone.isCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi` at Basic.lean:330 confirms the hypothesis is strictly stronger.
findings.fix: State it as `theorem IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.isBernsteinFunction_bernsteinPrimitive (hf : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f) (hcont : ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c)`, and derive the current `IsCompletelyMonotone` version (and `isBernsteinFunction_integral`) as one-line corollaries via `hf.isCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi` and `hf.contDiffOn.continuousOn`. Nonnegativity at the endpoint comes from `IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.nonneg` on `Ioi` plus `integral_nonneg_of_ae_restrict` (or a limit through `hcont`).
findings.issue: `isBernsteinFunction_bernsteinPrimitive` assumes `IsCompletelyMonotone f` (smooth up to 0), but the proof only ever uses `hf.contDiffOn.continuousOn`, `hf.nonneg`, and `hf.isCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi`. The Ici-class is a genuine strengthening — `Basic.lean` lines 22-25 explicitly note it excludes Laplace transforms such as `t ↦ ∫₀^∞ e^{-xt}(1+x)⁻²dx` — so the theorem misses the generic completely monotone function, including anything produced by the Bernstein–Widder representation (which yields only `IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi`).

findings.evidence: Bernstein/Basic.lean docstring lists `isBernsteinFunction_const` and `IsBernsteinFunction.add`; in the diff `hasDerivAt_bernsteinPrimitive` handles `c` solely via `.const_add c` and `deriv_bernsteinPrimitive`/`bernsteinPrimitive_eq` carry `{c : ℝ}` without using it.
findings.fix: Define `bernsteinPrimitive f t := ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..t, f (max x 0)` and state the `c`-version as a corollary using the existing `IsBernsteinFunction.add`/`isBernsteinFunction_const` closure lemmas, or at least drop `c` from the three derivative/value lemmas.
findings.issue: The initial value `c` is a parameter of the definition itself, so it propagates as a never-used argument through `bernsteinPrimitive_eq`, `hasDerivAt_bernsteinPrimitive`, and `deriv_bernsteinPrimitive` (in all three it is inert — the derivative and the `max`-congruence do not see it). `bernsteinPrimitive c f = (fun _ => c) + bernsteinPrimitive 0 f` is already obtainable from `isBernsteinFunction_const` and `IsBernsteinFunction.add`.

summary: The main theorem is stated for the strictly stronger closed-half-line class `IsCompletelyMonotone` although its proof only uses continuity on `[0,∞)` plus `IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi`; that excludes exactly the standard Bernstein-theory examples the project's own docstring names. The `c` parameter is also baked into the definition rather than derived from existing closure lemmas.
